date_note: Date of the arXiv preprint as stated by GBHackers (article published 24 November); the preprint itself was not read.
title: Researchers describe CAMEAR, an Android attack recovering speech from camera-interface motion data
summary: GBHackers reports a 20 November preprint by Guangyuan Ji, Wenjing Wang and Bingsheng Zhang describing CAMEAR. An Android app with camera permission could recover parts of speech played through the loudspeaker, using gyroscope data exposed through Camera2 rather than the microphone. GBHackers says the tests were controlled, yield partial transcription and document no attacks in the wild.
plain: Researchers say an Android app with camera permission could recover parts of speech played through a phone's speaker without microphone access, according to GBHackers. The tests were controlled and no real-world attacks are documented.
exec: GBHackers reports research showing camera permission may expose motion data that reveals speech; it documents no attacks in the wild.
action: General advice: review which apps hold camera permission and remove it where not needed; the authors, per GBHackers, recommend limiting motion metadata exposed to apps.

validation.note: Only GBHackers read; the arXiv preprint could not be found by search.
